quotes.text: Four and a half months is not a fortress. Seri. The cap stays.
quotes.author: — Shalini

quotes.text: The day Tara asks why we didn't take the bigger house… I'll show her the fortress.
quotes.author: — Shalini

chatMessages.text: Riya, the ₹1.85 one. Better layout, better tower. My eligibility covers it — the bank practically sang about it. Tell me why I'm hesitating.

Because your cap isn't set by eligibility — it's set by a memory. Thirty-eight percent, in the old life; you remember exactly what that felt like when things broke. Worst month at 24%: eleven months of buffer. At the ₹1.85 flat: four and a half. Test the cap as wisdom or scar tissue, and let the arithmetic hold.

tabs.insightTitle: What I noticed while we were searching
tabs.insightDescription: “Shalini's journey is deliberately low-amplitude — the drama is contained by design, because the discipline arrived first. The lawyer was hired before the broker; the settlement funds were documented before the first site visit; the will and guardianship were drafted before the shortlist existed. Her hardest moment wasn't a collapse — it was a better layout at ₹1.85 Cr that her eligibility could easily cover. We ran the worst-month simulation, and the cap held not because it scared her but because it taught her: eleven months of buffer at 24%, four and a half at the bigger flat. And the most human detail — Tara chose the finalists by which balcony could see the school van arrive. The morning-light kitchen and the van-visible balcony were the same flat. She'll show Tara the fortress someday.”
